digest.component_or_area: live jira dc harness test — provenance oracle
propositions: The provenance test asserts a raw Jira key (RBJNAZV-1) by substring scan against json.dumps(ticket), but the local id is lowercased (jira-rbjnazv-1) and the raw key is not present in the ticket payload unless it appears as a fallback summary, making the assertion impossible to pass even when inbound create works correctly.

The inbound create path builds the ticket payload from id/type/title/description/parent/tags/priority/assignee/creation_channel but does not include the raw Jira key in the payload; the key-to-id binding is recorded separately in the binding store, which list_tickets does not return.
The test must derive the expected local id using _jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key) and match against ticket.id exactly, not by substring scan, to assert what the inbound path actually produces.

The test must additionally assert that the binding store maps the derived local id to the remote_key, since that is where the DC↔local correspondence actually lives and where the headline acceptance criterion is substantiated.

Three sequential defects masked this oracle failure: empty store convergence, PAT-cap kill at setup, and the oracle itself unable to pass; only with all three fixed does the test's verdict carry information about whether inbound create actually works.
